Plot within- against between-subject dissimilarities

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotIndividuality.R, R/zzz-mae.R
plotIndividuality.Rd

plotIndividuality() compares the dissimilarities between samples of the same subject with those between samples of different subjects. The further apart the two distributions, the more individual the communities.

Usage

plotIndividuality(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
plotIndividuality(
  x,
  dissimilarity,
  group,
  layout = c("density", "box", "violin", "time"),
  group.by = NULL,
  time.col = NULL,
  facet.by = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotIndividuality(x, ..., experiment = 1L)

Arguments

x

a SummarizedExperiment object.

...

additional arguments passed to geom_density, geom_boxplot, geom_violin or, for layout = "time", geom_line.

dissimilarity

Character scalar. Specifies the sample by sample dissimilarity in metadata(x), as stored by mia::addDissimilarity().

group

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that identifies subjects.

layout

Character scalar. Draws density curves ("density"), box plots ("box"), violins ("violin") or the median and interquartile range in each time window ("time"). (Default: "density")

group.by

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that splits the between-subject pairs into pairs of the same and of different groups, such as the study centre. (Default: NULL)

time.col

Character scalar. For layout = "time", specifies the column from colData(x) holding the time window of each sample: a factor, or numeric, Date or POSIXct values of which each is one window. (Default: NULL)

facet.by

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that splits the pairs into panels. Only pairs of samples from the same group are kept. (Default: NULL)

experiment

Character scalar or integer scalar. For a MultiAssayExperiment, the experiment to plot; its samples get the colData of x. (Default: 1L)

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Each pair of samples is counted once. A subject with \(k\) samples gives \(k(k-1)/2\) within-subject pairs, so subjects sampled often weigh most in the within distribution.

With layout = "time", only pairs of samples from the same window are kept, and each line is the median dissimilarity of a kind of pair across the windows, as in Vatanen et al. (2018, doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0620-2, Fig. 2b). Make windows from times with cut().

Examples

data("hitchip1006", package = "miaTime")
tse <- hitchip1006
tse <- tse[, tse$subject %in% names(which(table(tse$subject) >= 2))]
tse <- mia::addDissimilarity(tse, method = "bray", assay.type = "counts")
plotIndividuality(tse, dissimilarity = "bray", group = "subject")


# By sex
plotIndividuality(tse, dissimilarity = "bray", group = "subject",
    layout = "box", facet.by = "sex")


# Across age windows, with pairs of subjects of the same and of
# different sex
tse$age.window <- cut(tse$age, c(18, 30, 40, 50, 60, 80),
    include.lowest = TRUE)
plotIndividuality(tse, dissimilarity = "bray", group = "subject",
    layout = "time", time.col = "age.window", group.by = "sex")
